claims.statement: The ci.yml workflow runs reusable test, lint, and documentation-link workflows plus merge-conflict, cross-reference, external documentation URL, and generated-file checks on pull requests and pushes to main.

The CI workflow uses GitHub's concurrency feature with group strategy to cancel earlier runs in favor of newer ones when multiple pushes occur to the same PR or branch, reducing queue time and resource usage.

The check-generated-files job in ci.yml verifies regenerated files match checked-in versions, with bypass capability via bypass-auto-check label and automatic skip for github-actions[bot] package download updates.

The scheduled package-download workflow keeps generation read-only until a second job consumes its short-lived artifact; when generated package and integration surfaces differ, that job creates a timestamped PR and enables squash auto-merge.

Package-download maintenance creates hosted-documentation candidate tickets only when both the required issue-service credential and team configuration are available; without either it runs candidate detection in dry-run mode.

The reusable test and lint workflows make shallow checkouts, synchronize the `test` dependency group, and run `make test` or `make lint` using caller-supplied Python and working-directory inputs; the reusable link workflow instead has read-only contents permission, a 20-minute limit, Python and Node setup, and runs Mintlify link and OpenAPI checks.

The external-integration pull_request_target workflow does not check out or execute PR code: it uses API file metadata and an organization-membership App token to label qualifying external integration PRs, reads added MDX as data to check featured frontmatter or download eligibility, and otherwise posts an idempotent listing-form redirect before closing the PR.

Integration submission automation begins only from manual dispatch or the integration-run label, verifies the triggering actor has write-level repository permission before checkout, and prevents duplicate processing with the integration-automation label.

After maintainer authorization, integration submission automation parses issue-form data as untrusted metadata and directs the agent to leave local edits only; parse, blocker, agent, and no-diff outcomes are reported on the issue, while a real diff alone lets the workflow create and link a review PR.

The package-download generator refreshes package counts only when their download timestamp is older than 24 hours, then regenerates the provider overview and integration download tables before artifact handoff.

The PR template asks contributors to describe the change and related work and, where applicable, confirm local documentation validation, tested examples, root-relative internal links, and navigation updates; it identifies preview deployment as an optional internal-team action.

The Mintlify preview workflow runs as pull_request or manual dispatch, creates and deploys a preview branch only for an in-repository PR or manual run, and grants write permissions only to the branch-writing and PR-commenting jobs.

When a pull request closes, preview cleanup derives a sanitized six-character source-branch prefix and deletes only remote branches matching that preview prefix after verifying that each branch begins with preview-.

The weekly changelog writer validates optional manual dates as a complete YYYY-MM-DD pair, serializes runs without cancellation, writes proposed entries to the summary in dry-run mode, and otherwise creates or updates a force-pushed review PR only when generated changelog state differs.

The credentialed code-sample workflow skips fork pull requests, runs all samples with tracing on scheduled or manual runs, and limits pull-request runs to changed supported sample files; a pull request with no such files is a successful no-op test step.

On full code-sample runs, trace-snippet regeneration requires a non-cancelled test step, fewer than 20 sample failures, and at least one refreshed trace; the writer stages only the trace manifest and generated snippet directory, exits on no diff, and appends to an existing standing PR or opens one on its dedicated branch.

The code-sample runner retries recognized rate limits and reports persistent ones as skipped rather than failed, but records ordinary sample failures as failures; trace collection is serialized, retries rate limits, and warns without failing an already successful sample when collection fails.

The scheduled onboarding-model workflow uses read-only repository contents and issue-write permission to compare remote LangSmith onboarding snippets; it fails on unreadable input, creates or updates one standing issue for drift, and closes that issue only when the checker returns clean.

The onboarding-model checker validates registry repository, ref, and source paths before fetching in-scope remote files, reports outdated supported provider model IDs with preferred replacements, and returns 0 when current, 1 on findings, or 2 when its registry or source is unreadable.

The weekly changelog workflow keeps its private pipeline report out of public repository surfaces: dry runs summarize only proposed entries, and review PR bodies use a generated summary and limited Vale output rather than the report.

The OpenWiki updater runs daily or manually, uses a full-history checkout so it can compare against the last documented commit, and limits its generated update PR to the wiki, repository instructions, and its workflow file.

docs-release-watch is a separate Managed Deep Agent project: it considers releases published 7–30 days earlier and creates one Linear DOC ticket and one draft documentation PR per needed feature; its OpenWiki coverage targets `src/oss/openwiki/`.

Integration submission serializes runs per issue without cancellation, and the agent is forbidden to push, open a pull request, or comment on GitHub so that the workflow retains ownership of repository mutations.

The weekly changelog workflow mints a GitHub App token for branch and PR operations, verifies force-push access before processing, and skips a same-day rerun rather than overwrite a changelog branch with commits not authored by the bot.

The weekly integration-repository workflow runs on Mondays at 09:15 UTC or manual dispatch with a 45-minute limit and only contents and pull-request write permissions; it invokes the checker in write mode, sends its evidence report to the job summary, and opens or updates a draft PR only when the working tree changes.

The integration-repository checker skips first-party langchain-ai homes, can repair a third-party GitHub home from live PyPI, npm, or external-docs evidence and permanent 301 or 308 documentation redirects, but leaves GitLab, partner-docs, malformed, failed-check, and first-party-replacement cases for attention; it proposes a delist only when no live GitHub, GitLab, or partner-docs alternative remains.

For a proposed integration delist, write mode removes the package record, matching external-listing entries and download rows, and only unshared provider cards; the generated evidence report separates applied changes, delists, attention cases, and errors and states that maintainers review the draft before merge.

The integration-repository workflow maintains one draft review PR on chore/dead-integration-repos: it snapshots changed files, restores them onto an existing open PR branch or a new branch, appends commits and refreshes evidence for an existing PR, and force-pushes only before creating a new draft PR.
